description:
🦕🍭 How Do Dinosaurs Say Trick or Treat? by Jane Yolen and Mark Teague is a delightful Halloween story that uses playful dinosaur characters to teach good manners and festive fun. The book follows a group of young dinosaurs as they prepare for and go out trick-or-treating. At first, readers see silly examples of what dinosaurs shouldn’t do—like grabbing too much candy, stomping on pumpkins, or scaring smaller kids. Then, the story shifts to show how well-behaved dinosaurs celebrate properly: they say “please” and “thank you,” share with friends, and enjoy the holiday with kindness and respect. Filled with bright, detailed illustrations and rhyming text, this story is perfect for preschool and early elementary children. Teachers and parents will appreciate its gentle reminders about manners, safety, and friendship, all wrapped up in a fun and lighthearted Halloween adventure.

description:
👻 Little Ghost Makes a Friend by Maggie Edkins Willis is a sweet and gentle story about friendship, bravery, and being yourself. The book follows Little Ghost, who is lonely and shy, living all by herself in an old house. She wants to make a friend but worries that her ghostly appearance might scare others away. One day, she meets a curious girl who isn’t frightened at all—in fact, she’s excited to meet a real ghost! As the two spend time together, Little Ghost learns that true friends accept you just as you are. With warm, expressive illustrations and a heartfelt message, this story helps young readers understand that kindness and courage can lead to unexpected friendships, making it a perfect read for the Halloween season without being spooky.

description:
🎃 The Good, the Bad, and the Spooky by Jory John and Pete Oswald is a humorous and heartwarming story that follows the Bad Seed as he prepares for Halloween. Normally full of confidence, the Bad Seed finds himself in a dilemma when he can’t decide on the perfect costume. Frustrated, he tries to cancel Halloween altogether, declaring that if he can’t look amazing, no one should celebrate. Through funny moments and colorful illustrations, readers watch as the Bad Seed learns an important lesson about letting go of perfection and embracing the fun of the holiday. By the end, he realizes that Halloween isn’t about having the best costume—it’s about enjoying time with friends, being creative, and having fun together. This story offers a relatable message for children about managing disappointment, sharing joy, and focusing on what really matters.

video_title: Leo The Late Bloomer: Kids read aloud_ Story time_ Kids books_ Toddler_ Reading_ Toddler time_ Book
description: 🐯Leo the Late Bloomer by Robert Kraus, illustrated by José Aruego, is a sweet story about patience, growth, and self-acceptance. The main character, Leo, is a young tiger cub who is slow to master many of the skills his friends—and his father—expect: he doesn’t read, write, draw well, eat neatly, or even talk. His father worries and watches anxiously, but Leo’s mother reassures him that Leo is simply a “late bloomer,” and that things happen in Leo’s own time. As the seasons pass and Leo isn’t forced, but gently given space, he gradually begins to blossom. Finally, one day he succeeds at all the things he once couldn’t do—and triumphantly declares, “I made it!” The book celebrates the idea that everyone develops at different rates and that confidence and growth often come when they’re not rushed.

description:
📖 Brown Bear, Brown Bear, What Do You See? Is written by Bill Martin Jr. and illustrated by Eric Carle. 

🐻 This story takes us on a fun, colorful journey where different animals appear one after another. Each page asks, “What do you see?” and the animal answers by describing the next animal in line. From a big brown bear to a red bird, a yellow duck, a green frog, and more—children get to meet a whole rainbow of creatures. At the end, the story circles back to children themselves, showing how they see all the animals together. It’s a simple, rhythmic, and predictable story that helps kids learn colors, animals, and patterns while keeping them engaged.
